content:
The reason to do this is twofold:

1. It gives them an OOT that they have no time-pressure to use and ergo they can learn about the (awesome) rewind mechanic when they need it. 
2. It allows them to gun for a OE or (ideally) AA standard character without waiting on Light to bestow an OOT at anniversary celebrations.

There's no guarantee that OOTs are handed out - BIAV could just decide tomorrow to retire the gift. But doing so would be painful to new players.

I would suggest making this a "special" OOT that has a tutorial attached when you use it that explains how to use it and why you'd want to. Maybe an "Enlightened Origin Of Time"? This OOT also should have no expiry time.

Giving everyone a guaranteed OOT means they can look into standard OEs and AAs and customize their account a bit, and help even out bad standard banner luck if they've had it. The main benefit for a smart player would be able to start targetting a key standard AA they want, like AA Caecus.

Instead of adding it to character level, it might be worth adding it to the Radix shop as a once-only purchase (or even as a purchase refreshed each time BIAV would normally gift one, so BIAV don't need to gift it?).

Disclaimer: I'm a new player (~2 months) so my understanding of the game could still be lacking.

Usually when playing a strategy game, I find myself looking at the boss's passive and skills to see if there are ways to work around them. Stuff like "Is there a way to make X attack less punishing?", "Is there a way to remove buff/debuff?", "Is there a way to prevent this attack that will wipe out my entire team?", etc... And I don't always find the answer to them every time. Sometimes you'll die, and it's fine. But when I find a built-in mechanic that allows me to deal with the boss better and utilize it and win, it feels good because I was rewarded by playing with the mechanics.

I think some of that is true in Morimens, but I keep feeling like there's not enough built-in boss mechanic to help you not being punished by a boss? Especially with GHelot who actively punishes you for playing cards... in a card game, and there is almost nothing you can do about it. There is no way to actively manage her fervor stack or reduce the damage she deals once she gets 10 stacks. Why can't it be something like:

- She gains stack if you play damaging card but loses stack if you play a defensive one maybe? Or symptom cards? Or non-damaging cards?
- If you play defense cards, she does X% less damage with attacks triggered by 10 fervor stacks? (Also I feel like most generic strike/defense cards are kinda useless ngl if you're not running a specific team, but what do I know)
